completion:
List the appliance's brand, model, and serial number.
3. Record the name, address, and contact information of the test property.
4. Document the date, time, and location of the test.
5. Identify the testing personnel and their qualifications.
6. Provide a checklist of the safety tests performed such as earth continuity, insulation resistance, polarity, and protective conductor size.
7. Clearly mark the test results for each safety check.
8. If a test fails, specify the test and the failure reason (e.g., high resistance, open circuit).
9. Take photographs of any visual damage or irregularities if applicable.

10. Include the identification of the faulty component, wiring, or connection if possible.
11. Note whether the appliance was operational at the time of testing.
12. Attempt a simple troubleshooting flow to document an attempt to fix minor issues.
13. Provide recommendations for repairs or replacement for the failed components.
